title: The canonical base-change mate is identity on an open isomorphism locus
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and use separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible commutative condensed coefficient of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For each scheme $T$ use the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$ and the canonical adjunction $a^*\dashv Ra_*$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]; pullback is exact by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Let $h:D\to Z$ be a morphism and $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Specify an identification $h^{-1}(U)\cong U$ under which $h|_{h^{-1}(U)}$ is $\mathrm{id}_U$, and let $i:U\hookrightarrow D$ be the resulting open inclusion. No properness or density hypothesis is imposed on $h$.

Let $v:Z'\to Z$ be any morphism in the setting. Put $D'=D\times_ZZ'$, $h':D'\to Z'$, $w:D'\to D$, $U'=U\times_ZZ'$, $v_U:U'\to U$, and let $j':U'\hookrightarrow Z'$, $i':U'\hookrightarrow D'$ be the open maps. The square $(h,h',v,w)$ is Cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let $\theta:h'^*v^*\xrightarrow{\sim}w^*h^*$ be the comparison induced termwise by module pullback composition [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp]. Define its derived mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] by
$$B_{h,K}=Rh'_*(w^*\varepsilon_{h,K})\circ Rh'_*(\theta_{Rh_*K})\circ\eta_{h',v^*Rh_*K}:v^*Rh_*K\longrightarrow Rh'_*w^*K.$$
There are canonical natural restriction isomorphisms $r_h:j^*Rh_*\xrightarrow{\sim}i^*$ and $r_{h'}:j'^*Rh'_*\xrightarrow{\sim}i'^*$, induced by the underived section identity $(h_*M)(V\to U)=M(V\to U\xrightarrow{i}D)$ and its primed version, using K-injective resolutions. Under these isomorphisms and the canonical pullback compositions $j'^*v^*\cong v_U^*j^*$ and $i'^*w^*\cong v_U^*i^*$, one has
$$j'^*B_{h,K}=\mathrm{id}_{v_U^*i^*K}$$
for every $K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_D})$, naturally in $K$. This asserts equality of the specified derived morphisms, without asserting that $B_{h,K}$ is an isomorphism before restriction.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-identity-open-underived-square-normalization] to the specified identity locus and its base change. This supplies the sectionwise $c_h,c_{h'}$, composition comparisons $a_h,a_{h'}$, their underived adjunct compatibility, and, writing $s:j'^*v^*\cong v_U^*j^*$ and $t:i'^*w^*\cong v_U^*i^*$, the derived termwise equation
$$t_{h^*A}\,i'^*(\theta_A)\,a_{h',v^*A}^{-1}=v_U^*(a_{h,A}^{-1})\,s_A.$$
The primed identity locus is $D'\times_{Z'}U'=h^{-1}(U)\times_UU'=U'$; hence all hypotheses hold for both triples.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-identity-open-derived-adjunction-normalization] separately to $(h,i,j)$ and $(h',i',j')$, using the underived adjunct compatibility just obtained. It gives the canonical K-injective natural restriction isomorphisms $r_h,r_{h'}$ of the statement and the actual derived equations
$$r_{h',h'^*A}\,j'^*(\eta_{h',A})=a_{h',A}^{-1},\qquad i^*(\varepsilon_{h,K})=r_{h,K}\,a_{h,Rh_*K}.$$
The lemma verifies the localized right-derived comparison units, so these formulas concern precisely the specified adjunctions.

source.place: Tag 0D6G, lemma-restrict-direct-image-open; Tag 08FI, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open; derived adjunct normalization via derived.tex, Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors and the existing derived adjoint-square comparison.

proof.text:
Expand the specified mate by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Naturality of $r_{h'}$ at $w^*\varepsilon_{h,K}$ and $\theta_{Rh_*K}$, followed by step 2's primed unit equation, gives
$$r_{h',w^*K}\,j'^*B_{h,K}=i'^*(w^*\varepsilon_{h,K})\,i'^*(\theta_{Rh_*K})\,a_{h',v^*Rh_*K}^{-1}.$$
Apply $t_K$, then its naturality, step 1's comparison equation, and step 2's unprimed counit equation:
$$\begin{aligned}
t_Kr_{h',w^*K}j'^*B_{h,K}
&=v_U^*(i^*\varepsilon_{h,K})\,v_U^*(a_{h,Rh_*K}^{-1})\,s_{Rh_*K}\\
&=v_U^*(r_{h,K})\,s_{Rh_*K}.
\end{aligned}$$
The last expression is the prescribed source identification and $t_Kr_{h',w^*K}$ the prescribed target identification. Composing with the inverse source identification proves the required identity. All factors are natural in $K$, for arbitrary unbounded $K$.
